newsitem.title: INDIA: India alliance's woes mount with "fodder" scandal.
newsitem.headline: India alliance's woes mount with "fodder" scandal.

text.p: Tension within Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's fractious coalition mounted on Wednesday after federal police received permission to prosecute the president of his party and a federal government minister.
Leftwing members of the 15-party coalition said they would push hard for the resignation of Janata Dal party president Laloo Prasad Yadav, who is also chief minister of the northern state of Bihar.
Bihar's governor on Tuesday authorised the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to pursue legal proceedings against Yadav in a $280 million corruption scandal over animal welfare funds.
Yadav says he is innocent and has repeatedly rejected demands that he resign from either post.
"I am not going to amend my stand, which I have already stated a number of times," the Times of India quoted Yadav as saying after the governor sanctioned his prosecution.
"I will fight the legal battle in the court and the political battle in the field. And I will not resign," he said.

The scandal dates back to the 1980s and involved the alleged siphoning off of funds for animal welfare projects. It broke last year when officials discovered large withdrawals from animal welfare accounts.
All India Radio said the governor's decision to allow the prosecution of Yadav had pushed the prime minister's party, already riven by bitter squabbling over a leadership election, into crisis.
The Pioneer newspaper quoted Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader Harkishen Singh Surjeet as saying Yadav had no moral authority to hold his posts.
The Marxist party is the second largest component of the United Front coalition. Gujral's Janata Dal is the largest.

"Mr Gujral will now be required to do a tightrope walk for, on the one hand, he is besieged by demands for Laloo Prasad Yadav's resignation and on the other, the Janata Dal leadership cannot crack the whip, considering Mr Yadav's standing both as a mass leader and being the Janata Dal president," the Times of India said.
Surjeet said he would also urge Gujral to sack junior Rural Areas and Employment Minister Chandradeo Prasad Varma, who the CBI says it plans to prosecute in connection with the same scandal.
All India Radio said the CBI investigations raised questions about the government's standing.
"At stake is the United Front's own credibility," the state-run radio station said in a commentary. "The Janata Dal needs to make an unambiguous statement that it stands for clean politics."
